espn-604002.headline: Eddie Jones wants to play his old house down
beats: Jones was England's long-time boss. He brings a young Japan side to Allianz Stadium chasing their first-ever win over England, and says he wants the "sky to fall in".

England arrive on three straight wins, the latest a 45-22 rout of Australia that was the most they have ever scored against them. Steve Borthwick has made 10 changes anyway, and only three players keep the same position from that side.
Japan lost 28-21 to Wales in Cardiff, close enough to make the point. A Japan win by 16 or more would push England down to sixth, below Scotland.

Jones claims England have one eye on New Zealand next. Maro Itoje has warned them not to "sleepwalk" into this one, which is the warning a side gives when it has noticed the fixture after this one too.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland meet a World Cup-winning coach a week early
beats: Jake White, who took South Africa to World Cup glory in 2007, started as Fiji coach last month. Warren Gatland and Shaun Edwards were reportedly also in the running. Ireland play South Africa on 21 November.
He inherits a side last of twelve with no points from four games, who conceded 54 to France last week. Captain Nathan Hughes is injured, so Peceli Yato takes the No 8 jersey and the armband.

Ireland beat Argentina 42–12 with six tries and sit level with England on 15 points. Andy Farrell has still made seven changes, with Jamison Gibson-Park back at scrum-half. Lose, and Ireland drop from third to fifth in the world.
White says there would be "nothing greater than for Fiji to host Ireland in Suva". For now, his side are the problem Ireland must solve before South Africa.

espn-604004.headline: Australia meet the Melbourne boy in Scotland's armband
beats: Sione Tuipulotu learned his rugby in a Melbourne backyard against Isaac Kailea, who went on to play for Australia. He says he will always have "that little bit of fire bubbling away" against them. Last weekend gave him a nearer grievance.

Scotland lost 21–43 to New Zealand at Murrayfield despite a hat-trick from hooker Ewan Ashman, and scored nothing after half-time. Australia know that scoreline. They lost to New Zealand by exactly that in October, then conceded 45 at Twickenham.
Les Kiss has made several changes. Joseph Suaalii moves back to outside centre and Carter Gordon returns. Win, and Australia take sixth in the world off Scotland.
Scotland won 27–13 when they last met, in 2024. Australia go to Wales next, and their captain's old neighbour would like them to arrive on four straight losses.

espn-604005.headline: Lost by 14 here last year, New Zealand need to win by 16
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at Allianz Stadium on 15 November 2025. This time a New Zealand win by 16 or more takes them past South Africa to 1st in the world.

Dave Rennie's side have scored 50, 43 and 43 in their last three, seven tries each time. England put 45 on Australia, a record win over them, and 73 on Fiji. Both teams have also conceded more than 40 to South Africa this year.
Frank Bunce has been impressed by the Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea centre pairing. England's midfield gets the closest look at it.
New Zealand do not play again until Chile at the World Cup in October 2027. Whatever ranking they take out of London, they will be looking at it for a long time.

espn-604006.headline: Japan keep losing by a converted try
beats: Japan's last two defeats were 28–21 to Wales in Cardiff and 34–28 to Fiji at home. Both opponents sit above them in the rankings, and neither got further away than seven points.
Scotland's last game at Murrayfield was a 43–21 loss to New Zealand, the same score Ireland put on them in March. Even their win in Argentina came with 38 points conceded.
Scotland start six places higher. Lose at all and they drop below Australia, which is the sort of thing a six-place gap is supposed to prevent.
Scotland have Italy at home in February. Japan have nothing scheduled, so a narrow defeat here would be the one they keep.

espn-604007.headline: Ireland's scrum has had a year to think about Dublin
beats: South Africa won 24–13 at the Aviva last November, and the scrum did most of it: six penalties from 16 scrums, a penalty try, and Ireland penalised ten times in the 12 that were not reset. Five Irish players were carded, James Ryan among them with a 20-minute red.

Andrew Porter was one of the yellows. Calf problems then kept him out of the Six Nations and the summer tour, which left that night as his last Test going into this month. His approach to the rematch is "Swing at it".

South Africa arrive off a 21–19 defeat in Paris. Ireland put six tries past Argentina in a 42–12 win. A home win would knock the world champions off the top of the rankings, with New Zealand the ones moving up.
Ireland have spent the autumn promising more fitness and better hands. This one asks about the front row first.

espn-604008.headline: Nine games, no wins between them, and now each other
beats: Italy have lost all five of their Nations Championship games and Fiji all four. Between them they are 291 points down, and Italy's one bonus point is the only thing either has banked.
Italy conceded 66 at home to South Africa on 7 November and 57 to Australia in July. Fiji let in 54 away to France that same weekend, so neither defence arrives in Udine with much to recommend it.

Fiji gave the job to Jake White last month, ahead of Warren Gatland and Shaun Edwards by reports. He won the 2007 World Cup with South Africa and has his eye on next year's. After this, Fiji's next game is Spain at that World Cup.
Win and Italy go up to ninth, above Fiji and Wales. Not bad going for a side that has lost five in a row.

espn-604009.headline: Even a draw with Argentina drops France out of fourth
beats: France have been fourth in the world since July and are unbeaten since a 34–32 loss in New Zealand. A draw here puts England above them, against a side with one win all year.
That win came against Wales. Argentina have added a draw with Australia, and their last outing ended 42–12 in Ireland.
France scored 54, 42 and 42 in three of their last four, then held on to beat South Africa 21–19 in Paris. They arrive heavily depleted but determined, by Rugbyrama's account.
France also won the last meeting, 37–23 in November 2024. Argentina's next game after this is against Canada at the World Cup in October 2027. That is a long time to sit on a result.

espn-604010.headline: Australia have conceded 138 in three. Cardiff is next.
beats: New Zealand put 50 and 43 on Australia in October, and England added 45 on 8 November. In September the same side beat South Africa 42–38, so the trouble is at the other end.

For Scotland, Les Kiss recalled Carter Gordon at fly-half, back from a broken leg, after Declan Meredith was dropped from the 23 following England. Australia have started seven different fly-halves since the last World Cup.

Wales beat Japan 28–21 at home with four tries and are much improved under Steve Tandy. They also lost 43–0 in South Africa in July, so neither defence arrives with a clean sheet. Win, and Wales go ninth while Australia slip below Argentina.
Australia still have the better points difference of the two. Wales have the better record, and the home crowd.
